source.title: Webhook Allowed Origins (CORS) entries after the first are broken when the list contains spaces

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
**Bug Description**

The webhook Allowed Origins (CORS) list is split on commas without trimming whitespace. With the common `https://a.com, https://b.com` spelling (comma followed by a space), every entry after the first keeps a leading space and never matches the request's `Origin` header. The response then carries the first entry instead of the requested origin, and the browser rejects the cross-origin response. Only the first entry of a space-separated list works.

Note: #18528 reported this symptom and was closed as fixed in n8n 1.109.0, but the origin-parsing code is unchanged on current master and the behavior still reproduces.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a workflow with a Webhook node (any response mode that answers the request, e.g. "When Last Node Finishes").
2. In the node options, set Allowed Origins (CORS) to `https://a.com, https://b.com` — note the space after the comma.
3. Activate the workflow and call the webhook with the header `Origin: https://b.com`.
4. Observe the response header: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://a.com` — the second, explicitly allowed origin was not matched and the browser blocks the response.
5. For comparison, configure the list without the space (`https://a.com,https://b.com`): `https://b.com` is matched and echoed. The whitespace alone changes whether an allowed origin works.

**Expected behavior**

Each comma-separated entry is trimmed before matching, so an origin listed as `https://a.com, https://b.com` matches requests from `https://b.com` and echoes it in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

**Debug Info**

```
n8nVersion: 2.49.0 (source build, master @ 75fe21cb)
database: sqlite
n8n_executions_mode: main
consumerId: n/a (local source build)
```

The behavior is server-side logic and is not specific to this environment.

## Environment

**Operating System:** Windows 11 (affects all platforms; the issue is in the CORS origin parsing, not platform-specific)

**n8n Version:** master @ 75fe21cb (2026-11-22), still present on current master (bf31087b); also present in the released 1.109.0 line despite #18528 being closed as fixed there

**Node.js Version:** 24.20.0

**Database:** SQLite (default)

**Execution mode:** main (default)

**Hosting:** self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The whitespace issue is in the production webhook handler: `packages/cli/src/webhooks/webhook-request-handler.ts` splits `allowedOrigins` on `,` and then uses `originsList.includes(req.headers.origin)` without trimming. So `https://b.com` cannot match the stored second entry ` https://b.com`; the fallback also uses the untrimmed first entry. Trimming each split entry before both matching and selecting the fallback would address both cases. A regression case for `https://a.com, https://b.com` in the webhook request-handler tests would pin this down.
